basis: Congenital nasal malformation; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Combined deficiency of coagulation factors VIII, IX and XI.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; no common direct damage to another organ is established.
Benign neoplasm arising from blood vessels; anatomical sites vary across this umbrella.
Melanoma originating in the posterior uvea.
Inherited epilepsy with febrile and afebrile seizures; additional developmental manifestations remain neurologic.
Adenocarcinoma originating in extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Bone sclerosis causes marrow failure (anemia 3/6), visual impairment (2/5) and hypocalcemia (3/6). Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Retinal vascular disease with potential scarring and detachment; prematurity does not establish other organ involvement.
Nonsyndromic congenital hearing loss with cochlear and vestibular malformations.
Urinary reflux and collecting-system abnormalities define the disease. UTIs are separate infections; hypermobility alone does not establish locomotor tissue damage.
Motor neuron disease causes progressive muscle atrophy in essentially all patients. Diaphragmatic weakness affects skeletal muscle rather than lung tissue.
Direct manifestations include arthritis (~80%), inflammatory skin disease (~70%) and nephritis (~40%); common cytopenias and oral ulcers omitted by the four-axis cap.
Nonsyndromic hearing loss with vestibular dysfunction; speech delay secondary to deafness does not establish brain disease.
Primary developmental brain disorder; tooth agenesis occurs in 80-99% and alternating esotropia in 30-79%. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Severe developmental delay, diabetes and osteoporosis/osteosarcoma characterize the syndrome. Cataracts are a defining feature, with frequency unreported; macrocytosis alone is not injury.
Scrotal reproductive-system disorder; no covered organ is specified across this umbrella.
Glutathione metabolism defect; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2. Asthma and eczema are separate diagnoses; incontinence does not establish urinary tract injury.
Direct lesion of the sciatic peripheral nerve.
Characteristic follicular skin tumors; pulmonary cysts affect ~80% and predispose to pneumothorax. Renal carcinoma is a separately diagnosed tumor risk.
Cerebral motor disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish intrinsic skeletal muscle damage.
Localized amyloid deposition produces cutaneous disease; systemic organ involvement is not characteristic.
Lipoprotein clearance disorder causing chylomicronemia. Pancreatitis is a separate complication; splenomegaly alone does not establish functional injury or autoimmune disease.
Parotid salivary malignancy; perineural tumor invasion directly occupies nerves in roughly 40-70% of cases.
Benign neoplasm originating in breast parenchyma; breast has no axis.
